questions.problem:
Find a normal vector to the plane

$$
r=⟨1,1,0⟩+t⟨-1,1,1⟩+s⟨0,2,2⟩,\,t,\,s\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
questions.worked_solution:
From the parametric equation, we have that $v=⟨-1,1,1⟩$ and $w=⟨0,2,2⟩$ are parallel to the plane.

Now, we need to find a normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of $v$ and $w$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =v\times w \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =2j-2k \\  & =⟨0,2,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨0,2,-2⟩.$

questions.problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point $H(-3,2,7)$ and is parallel to the lines $r=⟨3,-1,20⟩+s⟨-3,0,1⟩$ and $r=⟨0,3,-4⟩+t⟨2,1,-\frac{1}{5}⟩.$
questions.worked_solution:
The direction vectors of the lines are ${v}_{1}=⟨-3,0,1⟩$ and ${v}_{2}=⟨2,1,-\frac{1}{5}⟩$, respectively. These vectors are parallel to the plane but not to each other.

We also know that the point $H(-3,2,7)$ lies on the plane and its position vector is $h=⟨-3,2,7⟩.$  

So, the corresponding parametric equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =h+s{v}_{1}+t{v}_{2} \\ r & =⟨-3,2,7⟩+s⟨-3,0,1⟩+t⟨2,1,-\frac{1}{5}⟩,\,s,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the points $D(1,0,-2),\,E(-2,-2,5)$, and $F(-2,4,3).$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we need to find two vectors that are parallel to the plane (but not to each other). Let's use the displacement vectors $\overset{\to }{DE}$ and $\overset{\to }{DF},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{DE} & =⟨-2,-2,5⟩-⟨1,0,-2⟩ \\  & =⟨-3,-2,7⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{DF} & =⟨-2,4,3⟩-⟨1,0,-2⟩ \\  & =⟨-3,4,5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, if we consider the position vector $d=⟨1,0,-2⟩$ of the point $D,$ then the corresponding parametric equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =d+s\overset{\to }{DE}+t\overset{\to }{DF} \\ r & =⟨1,0,-2⟩+s⟨-3,-2,7⟩+t⟨-3,4,5⟩,\,s,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find a normal vector to the plane

$$
r=⟨3,\sqrt{7},-2⟩+t⟨-2,8,0⟩+s⟨3,-1,-1⟩,\,t,\,s\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
questions.worked_solution:
From the parametric equation, we have that $v=⟨-2,8,0⟩$ and $w=⟨3,-1,-1⟩$ are parallel to the plane.

Now, we need to find a normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of $v$ and $w$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =v\times w \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 8 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -2 & 8 & 0 \\ 3 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =-8i-2j-22k \\  & =⟨-8,-2,-22⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨-8,-2,-22⟩.$
